name: ElevenLabs
tagline: AI voice generation, dubbing, speech-to-text, and voice tools

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Creator listed at $22/month, with lower Starter and higher Pro tiers.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 10,000 credits/month, roughly 10 minutes of standard text-to-speech in the web app; no rollover

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 30,000 credits/month, roughly 30 minutes of standard text-to-speech

tiers.name: Creator
tiers.limits: 121,000 credits/month, roughly 121 minutes of standard text-to-speech
tiers.notes: First month is advertised at $11; annual equivalent is based on $220/year.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 600,000 credits/month, roughly 600 minutes of standard text-to-speech

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: 1.8 million credits/month, roughly 1,800 TTS minutes, and 3 seats

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 6 million credits/month, roughly 6,000 TTS minutes, and 10 seats

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom credits, seats, concurrency, security, and support

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free plan: 10,000 credits/month (about 10 standard TTS minutes), 15 included Agents minutes, 4 Agents concurrency, and 0 credit rollover.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual plans charge 10 months for 12; usage top-ups and pay-as-you-go are separate
pricing.hiddenCosts: Credit burn varies sharply: STT is 330 credits/minute, music 900/minute, SFX 200/generation, voice changer/isolator 1,000/minute, and dubbing 2,000-10,000/minute. Paid rollover is capped at two extra months and is forfeited on downgrade/cancel. PAYG top-ups start at $5, can auto-top-up, are nonrefundable, and expire after 12 months. Agents overages are $0.08/minute, burst concurrency $0.16/minute, plus telephony/LLM charges.

verdictSummary: A TTS wrapper is easy, but high-quality voice models, voice cloning safety, dubbing workflows, licensing, and compute are the product.
coreLoopDIY: Build a text-to-speech UI around an open model or API, store generated files, and expose voice presets.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for convincing voices, controls, and commercial workflow reliability.

priorArt.name: OpenVoice
priorArt.desc: Open-source voice cloning/TTS research implementation; useful prior art but not full SaaS

alternatives.name: pyVideoTrans
alternatives.desc: Drop in a video and it does the dull chain, transcribe, translate, dub, remux, without billing by the minute.

facts.install: Download the prepackaged Windows archive, unzip it to a simple path and run sp.exe; source and Docker paths exist for other platforms
facts.engines: ASR via faster-whisper/Whisper, WhisperX, Parakeet and cloud APIs; translation via DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, MiniMax, Ollama/M2M100 and others; TTS via Edge-TTS, F5-TTS, CosyVoice, GPT-SoVITS, ChatTTS, Chatterbox, OpenAI/Azure and others
facts.dataFormat: Source media, SRT subtitles, generated audio/video and configuration files in local output/config folders; selected cloud APIs receive the relevant media or text
facts.gapVsPaid: It automates a broad dubbing chain, but voice quality, timing consistency and workflow reliability vary sharply with the chosen local models and APIs.
facts.setupBlocker: The Windows build wants a path without spaces or non-ASCII characters; GPU acceleration needs matching CUDA/cuDNN, and some backends need API keys

alternatives.name: TTS WebUI
alternatives.desc: A 10GB local voice lab with an installer and every model drawer open; model licences are your homework.

facts.install: On Windows install TTS WebUI Ignition with winget; otherwise use a release/legacy installer or Docker
facts.engines: Extension-driven local models including Bark, Tortoise, MMS, Vall-E X, StyleTTS2, SeamlessM4T, XTTSv2, F5-TTS, Parler-TTS, OpenVoice, Kokoro, DIA, CosyVoice, GPT-SoVITS, Piper and Chatterbox
facts.dataFormat: Downloaded model caches, generated audio files and metadata in local installation/data directories; SQLite can hold generated-audio metadata
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks ElevenLabs' consistent managed quality, production API and turnkey dubbing, while model licenses and GPU compatibility become the user's problem.
facts.setupBlocker: The base install is about 10.7 GB, models add several gigabytes each, and GPU/CUDA or extension dependency conflicts are common

alternatives.name: Voicebox
alternatives.desc: A local voice studio with cloning, seven engines, transcription and a multi-track editor; dubbing still takes manual assembly.

facts.install: Install the macOS DMG or Windows MSI; Docker is supported, while Linux currently requires a source installation
facts.engines: Qwen3-TTS, Qwen CustomVoice, LuxTTS, Chatterbox Multilingual, Chatterbox Turbo, HumeAI TADA and Kokoro; Whisper/Whisper Turbo for speech-to-text; local Qwen3 models for refinement and personas
facts.dataFormat: SQLite plus model, voice-profile, generated-audio and capture files in the local Voicebox data directory; original audio and transcripts stay on device
facts.gapVsPaid: It has no turnkey multilingual video translation and dubbing pipeline, and output consistency depends on the local engine and hardware.
facts.setupBlocker: Large model downloads and choosing a hardware backend; Linux has no prebuilt binary yet

rejectedAlternatives.name: AllTalk TTS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Feature-rich, but the maintained work lives off the stale main branch and installation still starts with Git, Python and C++ tools.

notes: Strong no; model and safety moat are structural.
prompt:
Build me a personal text-to-speech workbench, the DIY slice of ElevenLabs.
Requirements:

- A Node CLI plus a small local web page (Express, localhost only): paste text,
  pick a voice preset, get an mp3.
- Engine 1: Piper or Kokoro running locally on CPU, free and private. Engine 2:
  optional OpenAI TTS fallback, key in .env, for when quality beats privacy.
- Save every generation to ~/TTS/YYYY-MM-DD/<slug>.mp3 with a sidecar .txt
  holding the input text plus the engine and voice used.
- Voice presets in voices.json: name, engine, voice id, speed.
- Batch mode: point it at a folder of .txt files, get a folder of mp3s, for
  narrating notes or articles.
- No accounts, no telemetry, local-first; the only network calls are the
  optional hosted API.
- Out of scope: voice cloning, dubbing, and emotional voice direction. Never
  clone a real person's voice; that is exactly the part that should not be DIY.
- README: model download steps, and state honestly that the voice quality gap
  versus ElevenLabs is real; frontier voice models plus licensing are the
  product and cannot be rebuilt solo.
